pullQuote: A2UI is my pick: agents emit schema-validated UI data, not code, and renderers for React, Flutter and SwiftUI draw it natively.
testimonial: I'd choose A2UI. Its UI-as-data protocol, schema validation and developer-controlled widget catalog give agents a hard capability boundary, and it has renderers for web (React, Lit, Angular) and native (Flutter, SwiftUI). The trade-off is that A2UI is not a visual design system. Compared with Tamagui, or with shadcn/ui on top of Base UI, you still have to supply the human-facing components and branding. Its roadmap lists templates and sandboxed logic as future work, so some pieces are unfinished. I only read the README, so I haven't verified how mature each renderer is.
evaluations:
**Tamagui** — A style library plus optimizing compiler that shares code across React and React Native. It flattens styled components to a `div` with atomic CSS on web, or to a View on native ([README](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui)). It is a strong choice for human-facing web and native UI. The README mentions nothing agent-facing, such as a schema or catalog. That is a gap in the README, not proof the project lacks it. Agents would need to be wired in separately, for example by putting Tamagui components behind an A2UI catalog.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — Unstyled accessible React components and hooks (React Aria), Adobe's Spectrum implementation, and React Stately, which the README says can be used on other platforms like React Native. It also includes internationalization for 30+ languages ([README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). The behavior and accessibility layer is excellent. It is a web library with no agent protocol, so it would sit under an agent-facing layer.

**MCP Apps** — An MCP extension where tools declare `ui://` HTML resources that the host renders in a sandboxed iframe, with two-way messaging. It ships agent skills for scaffolding, and Claude, ChatGPT and VS Code are listed as supported hosts ([README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps)). The UI is HTML in an iframe, not native widgets. It is a good delivery channel but not a design system.

**MUI** — Material UI is a React implementation of Material Design, extended by MUI X ([README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui)). It is mature, but the README describes a React-only library with no agent or native story.

**shadcn/ui** — Copy-in, open-code components you own and customize ([README](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui)). Its registry format is reused by Ouro UI and AI Elements. It is web only and has no agent protocol of its own. json-render ships a 36-component shadcn catalog, which is one way to give it an agent surface.

**json-render** — A Vercel Labs generative-UI framework. You define a Zod catalog of components and actions, the model emits JSON, and renderers draw it. Renderers cover React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and React Native, plus an MCP package ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). It is conceptually close to A2UI. It is a single-vendor labs project, and I saw no SwiftUI or Compose renderers listed. Native coverage is therefore React Native only.

**Vercel UI SDK** — A beta library of framework-agnostic behaviors (focus, selection, popups, ARIA) with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components, and an agent skill ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui)). It is aimed at agents authoring components. It is beta, ships no visual design, and has no native targets.

**Radix UI** — Low-level accessible web primitives, usable as the base layer of a design system ([README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). It is web only with no agent surface.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — Tailwind 4 tokens and Radix-based React components tuned for ChatGPT apps ([README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui)). It is useful inside ChatGPT. It is tied to that host and has no native support.

**Base UI** — An unstyled accessible component library from the creators of Radix, Floating UI and Material UI ([README](https://github.com/mui/base-ui)). It is a good web primitive layer, and Ouro HX builds on it. The README mentions no agent or native features.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — A framework where each action is defined once and used by the agent as a tool and by the UI as a function, exposed over HTTP, MCP, A2A and CLI ([README](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native)). The shared-action design is strong. It is an application framework rather than a design system, and I saw no native renderers.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — A declarative UI framework across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS, with built-in accessibility and localization ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)). It is excellent for Apple platforms but has no web story. A2UI's SwiftUI renderer is the path to drive it from agents.

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's web library: React v9, React v8, and Web Components ([README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui)). It is mature and used in Microsoft 365. It targets web only, and the README mentions no agent features.

**Ouro UI** — Shadcn-registry React components built on Base UI, plus a built-page check for overlap, axe-core violations and similar issues. It has an agent-facing half called Ouro AX and an llms.txt ([README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui)). It is web only, and from the README it looks like a young project. I did not read the Ouro AX section.

**A2UI** — An open Apache 2.0 protocol where agents emit validated UI data instead of code. Renderers exist for Lit, Angular, React, Flutter and SwiftUI. There are agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript and Dart, A2A and ADK glue, and an MCP catalog ([README](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui)). Trade-offs: it supplies a widget catalog but not a branded design system. The roadmap still lists templates and sandboxed logic as future work. I did not check renderer maturity.

**AI Elements** — Chat components built on shadcn/ui. The README says it will be deprecated at the end of November 2026 in favor of a shadcn/ui version ([README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). That is a reason not to start a new project on it.

**Chakra UI** — Accessible React components with an MCP server for Cursor ([README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)). It is web only. The MCP server helps coding agents, but it does not let agents drive runtime UI.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — Material 3 components and theming for Compose, covering Android and the form factors in its docs ([docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)). It is strong on Android only. A2UI's catalog or a Flutter renderer would be needed for cross-platform agent output.

**Flutter** — Google's single-codebase SDK for mobile, web and desktop, with Material and Cupertino widget sets ([README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter)). It draws its own pixels instead of using native widgets. A2UI has a Flutter renderer. That makes Flutter a strong rendering target, but on its own it has no agent layer.

**CopilotKit** — An agent-to-UI stack on the AG-UI protocol. It offers chat components, generative UI (including A2UI specs and MCP Apps), shared state and human-in-the-loop, across React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack and Teams ([README](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). It is strong for agent integration. It is a runtime and chat stack, not a design system, and I saw no SwiftUI or Compose targets.
